The mechanism involves intratumoral delivery of IL-12 plasmid DNA via electroporation, but no direct evidence of IL-12 protein expression or immune activation markers were reported. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to confirm downstream immune activation or anti-tumor immunity stimulation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met across all three arms with ORR of 32.1% (main study), 25% (regimen A), and 25% (regimen B). These response rates are clinically meaningful for melanoma. The treated vs untreated lesion analysis provides strong evidence of local efficacy - treated lesions showed consistently higher regression rates (64%, 60%, 25%) compared to untreated lesions (31.8%, 38.5%, 50%) in most comparisons. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial enrolled unselected melanoma patients. The treated vs untreated lesion comparison suggests the mechanism works locally where the therapy is applied. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm trial without control group makes it difficult to rule out natural disease fluctuation or other confounders, but the consistent benefit in treated vs untreated lesions within the same patients provides internal validation.
